name: FOCAS Lab
full_name: Formal Control and Autonomous Systems Lab
intro: We design controllers for robots and cyber-physical systems that come with formal guarantees: robust, reliable, and safe by construction. Our work spans theory and hardware, from temporal-logic specifications and spatiotemporal tubes to learning-based control and multi-robot systems.
address: FOCAS Lab, Department of Cyber-Physical Systems
TCS Smart X Hub, Indian Institute of Science

research.title: Safe Autonomy
research.text: Autonomous cars, aircraft and robots promise fewer collisions and less congestion, but only if their safety and correctness can be certified. We synthesize controllers with formal guarantees for complex tasks given as temporal-logic specifications.

research.title: Learning-based Control
research.text: Many cyber-physical systems lack precise models. We use data-driven and machine-learning methods, such as neural certificates, Gaussian processes and conformal prediction, to give probabilistic and formal guarantees for unknown dynamical systems.

research.title: Multi-Robot Systems
research.text: Teams of robots must reach consensus, hold formations, stay connected and avoid collisions using distributed resources. We develop scalable, provably safe controllers for multi-agent systems under sensing and communication constraints.

research.title: Constrained Nonlinear Control
research.text: Performance limits, input saturation, physical stops and safety specifications all constrain real systems. We design approximation-free, real-time controllers, including funnel and spatiotemporal-tube methods, that respect these constraints by construction.

research.title: Cyber-Physical Systems
research.text: CPS couple computation with physical processes, giving hybrid models with discrete transitions and continuous dynamics. We build symbolic abstractions and compositional synthesis methods that keep controller design tractable at scale.

courses.title: Applied Linear and Nonlinear Control
courses.text: A postgraduate course linking advanced control theory to robots, with MATLAB, Simulink, ROS 2 and motion-capture experiments. It covers linear and nonlinear dynamics, stability theory, optimal control and safety-critical control, and ends with controllers running on mobile robots and manipulators.

openings.title: PhD / M.Tech (Research)
openings.text: Apply to the Department of Cyber-Physical Systems through IISc admissions. Windows open in March–April and September–October.

openings.title: Postdoctoral research
openings.text: For PhD holders, including those who have submitted their thesis, with experience in control, robotics, formal methods, ML or RL. Funding routes include the IoE / C. V. Raman PDF, NPDF and DS Kothari fellowships.

openings.title: Research internships
openings.text: For undergraduates in EE, ECE, CS, ME, robotics or applied mathematics. The INSA Summer Research Fellowship and FAST-SF usually open in October–November.
